$schema-note: The framework's wiring, declared ONCE. `tools/wiring-generate.js` turns this into the hook declarations a harness executes; `test/wiring-drift-gate.test.js` regenerates and compares against the LIVE file. See docs/framework/wiring-manifest.md.

harness.name: claude-code
harness._why_harness: WHAT VARIES BETWEEN HARNESSES, DECLARED AS DATA. `wiring-plan.js` decides (frame coordinates, the state lane, the bound, ownership) and it is SHARED; this block says how THIS harness writes a wiring down — its serialization format, the events it has, and where a declaration lives in its document. That split is what makes a THIRD harness cost ONE MANIFEST and ZERO engine lines: a generator that learned one special case per product would be a TOOL, and the founding rule of this project is that the engine must not move when a need appears. 🛑 There is no default: assuming one product's shape for another writes a document that harness reads as nothing at all, with no error and no log.
harness._why_events: THE EVENT NAMES ARE THIS HARNESS'S OWN, and they are mapped rather than assumed. A harness that spells them differently declares the spelling here; a harness that LACKS one has no entry, and every consumer on that event is SKIPPED and NAMED by the generator — never bodged onto a neighbouring event, and never dropped in silence, because a path missing from a wiring looks exactly like one that works.
harness._why_layout: WHERE OUR DECLARATIONS LIVE IN THE DOCUMENT AND WHAT EVERY FIELD IS CALLED. `container` is the path, `{event}` being the segment that branches per event; `grouping: "blocks"` nests entries under a matcher-carrying block; `fields` maps this framework's declaration fields onto this harness's key names. 🛑 A field the layout names NO key for is a NAMED REFUSAL, never a silent drop: a dropped bound, matcher or endpoint produces a wiring that RUNS and differs from what was declared, which is the one failure mode this repository refuses outright. ⚠️ `write.mode: "splice"` is admissible here because this shape is the one `wiring-plan.splice` walks — JSON it can re-read and compare byte for byte, blocks carrying a matcher, a container branching on the event. That is a property of the LAYOUT and never of a product: any harness shaped this way gets the write mode for free, and any other gets the fragment mode with its written reason.

_why_transport: WHICH TRANSPORT CARRIES THE GATE'S LANE - it is a property of the WIRING, so it belongs here and nowhere else. `kind: "http"` turns each of the N frames into a local POST to the already-running daemon instead of a ~330 ms node start (5,300 ms -> 182 ms per action at 16 frames, MEASURED 2026-08-22); the frame coordinates then travel in the query (`?frame=k&frames=N`) instead of in argv, and `bounds.gateHookTimeoutSeconds` becomes the bound of that POST. Claude Code 2.1.237 really implements `type:"http"` (verified IN the binary). `kind: "command"` is the DEFAULT when this key is absent, and it stays the only form Codex can run ('Only type:"command" handlers run today') - a port of this manifest to that harness declares it, it does not patch the generator. An UNKNOWN kind is a NAMED REFUSAL, never a quiet fall back to a spawn: a harness with no handler for a transport runs NOTHING for those declarations, with no error and no log. NEITHER THE ADDRESS NOR THE ROUTE IS DECLARED HERE, AND THAT IS THE FIX OF 2026-08-25, TAKEN IN TWO GESTURES THE SAME DAY. The host and the port were `transport.host` and `transport.port` while the daemon that BINDS them held a `HOST` and a `DEFAULT_PORT` constant of its own; the ROUTE was `transport.path` while the daemon that SERVES it held `/pretool` in `src/hooks/state-client.js` and its three sibling routes as constants of `src/hooks/http-server.js`. ONE truth, TWO places, FOUR times over, agreeing by luck with nothing comparing them - the class of the 2026-08-22 split brain, on a lane with NO fallback where a single divergence loses every frame of every action in silence. THE ROUTE IS THE WORST OF THE FOUR: a wrong host or port fails at the socket, while a misspelt route SUCCEEDS - the daemon serves the GATE route for any path it does not recognise, so the frames would be answered by a route nobody meant and nothing anywhere would be red. A listening address is ONE fact, so it is ONE key: `http: { host, port }` in `ctxroute-config.json`, resolved WHOLE at the single point `paths.httpEndpoint()` that the daemon reads too. A route name is a fact of our PROTOCOL, so its owner is the module that knows nothing else: `src/protocol-routes-pure.js`, imported by the daemon, by the four client shells and by `tools/wiring-generate.js`. Both reach `plan()` as MACHINE FACTS (DERIVE, NEVER ENUMERATE - exactly as `frames` already did). Re-declaring any of them here would rebuild the divergence inside the very file that exists to remove it, so an unknown key of this object is a NAMED REFUSAL and not an ignored one. What stays in this manifest is what belongs to the WIRING and to nothing else: which transport carries the frames. On this transport the gate carries NO lane argument: the daemon IS the authority, and its three disk-bound peers keep `--client` - that asymmetry is exactly what `doctor.js --settings` checks for split brain.

bounds._why_gateHookTimeoutSeconds: A BOUND, NOT A WAIT — it makes nobody patient, it refuses to wait for ever. MEASURED 2026-08-22: a POST to the daemon over the loopback answers in 11 ms, over 16 and over 100 sequential frames, connection reused. Ten seconds is roughly 900x that measurement, so no load this machine can produce turns a healthy answer into a false positive; a number chosen at 2x or 5x would be an ATTENTION budget and would fire on a busy machine. WHAT IT ACTUALLY BOUNDS: a daemon that HANGS — accepted the connection and never answered. It NEVER bounds a daemon that is DEAD: a refused connection comes back instantly as ECONNREFUSED, from the kernel, and no delay of any kind is involved in that path. That distinction is also why this value does NOT belong in temporal-budget.json, which excludes this exact class by name ('an option key named timeout is a BOUND, not a WAIT', 40 occurrences already set aside): enrolling a bound there would demand one of the two admissible motives (distant / undecidable) for something that waits for nothing, i.e. an invented justification. Declared HERE, ONCE, because the alternative is the harness default applied in silence — 60 s on the command lane and 600 s on the http lane (see HOOK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULTS in src/harness-profile.js), a choice nobody in this repository ever made.
